title: Best GDPR Compliance Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare GDPR compliance tools on cookie consent, data mapping, impact assessments, subject rights, multi-law support and ease of setup.
intro: Choosing the right GDPR compliance tool can save your business from hefty fines and simplify privacy management. This page compares four platforms on cookie consent, data mapping, impact assessments, subject rights, multi-law support and ease of setup.

products.name: OneTrust
products.tagline: Privacy management platform for large organizations
pros: Consent, data mapping, assessments and subject rights in one platform
Cookie consent banners and preference centers
cons: Quote-only pricing aimed at large organizations
Complex to set up; expect training

products.name: Cookiebot
products.tagline: Cookie consent banner and scanner for websites
products.pricing: Free for one domain up to 50 subpages; Premium plans from €7/month
cons: No impact assessments or request workflows

products.name: TrustArc
products.tagline: Privacy compliance platform for assessments, consent and requests
pros: Assessment templates and questionnaires for DPIAs
Covers GDPR and other major privacy laws
cons: Quote-only pricing aimed at larger businesses
Takes time to set up, like other enterprise platforms

products.name: iubenda
products.tagline: Privacy policy generator and cookie banner for websites
products.pricing: Free plan available; paid plans from €4.99/month billed yearly
pros: Good for small to medium businesses

verdict.summary: OneTrust scores highest on this page's six criteria, covering consent, data mapping, impact assessments and subject rights, though, like TrustArc, it takes work to set up. TrustArc is second, matching OneTrust on impact assessments, subject rights and multi-regulation support, with less complete consent and data-mapping tools. Cookiebot and iubenda tie well behind them (Cookiebot is listed first alphabetically): both are easy to install and have free plans, but they focus on cookie consent and policies rather than full GDPR programs, and neither offers impact assessments.

bestFor.useCase: Large enterprises with complex privacy needs
bestFor.reason: Highest score here, with the most complete feature set
Assessment templates for DPIAs, plus automated subject-rights handling

bestFor.useCase: Small to medium websites needing cookie compliance
bestFor.reason: Easy implementation with automatic cookie scanning and a free plan for small sites

bestFor.useCase: Startups and small businesses on a budget
bestFor.reason: User-friendly setup, policy generator, free plan and low-cost paid tiers

pro_tips: Start with a free trial or demo to test the platform's ease of use before committing to enterprise pricing plans.
Open your site in a private window to see your cookie banner as a first-time visitor with no saved preferences.
Ensure your chosen tool can handle cookie consent for all third-party services you use, not just basic analytics cookies.
Look for tools that offer automatic updates when privacy laws change - manual compliance updates are time-intensive and error-prone.
Choose a solution that grows with your business rather than starting with the most basic option if you plan to expand internationally.

faqs.question: Do I need a GDPR compliance tool if I'm a small business?
faqs.answer: GDPR applies to businesses of all sizes that process the personal data of people in the EU, so small businesses need to comply too, though not necessarily with a paid tool. A compliance tool can help automate cookie consent and reduce your risk of fines, which can reach €20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

faqs.question: What's the difference between cookie consent and full GDPR compliance?
faqs.answer: Cookie consent is just one part of GDPR compliance. Full compliance includes data mapping, privacy policies, subject rights management, breach notifications, and privacy by design principles.

faqs.question: Can I use multiple tools together for GDPR compliance?
faqs.answer: Yes, many businesses use specialized tools for different aspects - like Cookiebot for consent management and a separate tool for data subject requests. Just ensure they integrate well together.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for GDPR compliance tools?
faqs.answer: Cookie consent can start free: Cookiebot and iubenda both have free plans for small sites, and their paid plans start at a few euros a month. Enterprise platforms such as OneTrust and TrustArc are priced by quote, and costs rise with the number of sites, users and modules you need.

faqs.question: Do these tools guarantee GDPR compliance?
faqs.answer: No tool can guarantee 100% compliance as GDPR requirements depend on your specific data processing activities. These tools help implement technical measures, but you still need proper policies and procedures.
